title: Invalid network certificate error UX could be improved
line: The weather widget no longer pops up a certificate warning dialog when its provider's certificate can't be verified; it shows its own error message instead.
explanation: The weather providers (Open-Meteo, NOAA, Environment Canada, DWD, BBC) download their data with plain KIO jobs from inside plasmashell. When the TLS certificate fails to verify (a broken Qt/OpenSSL package, a captive portal, a provider's expired certificate), KIO's HTTP worker asks the user with the modal "Server Authentication" dialog, and it does so again on every refresh. The change sets KIO's ssl_no_ui metadata on every provider request, the same way KIO's own favicon fetcher does, so the request simply fails and the widget shows its existing "Unable to load weather forecast" message.

commits.message:
applets/weather: don't ask about invalid certificates

When a weather provider's certificate failed to verify, every refresh
popped up KIO's modal certificate dialog over the desktop. The providers'
requests now skip that dialog and fail, so the widget shows its error.

BUG: 446328

media.caption: Open-Meteo served with an untrusted certificate: plasmashell pops up the modal "Server Authentication" dialog over the desktop.
Same setup with the fix: no dialog, the widget shows "Unable to load weather forecast".

reviews.text: Setting KIO's ssl_no_ui metadata on all five weather ions cleanly stops the weather widget from popping up modal certificate dialogs and lets it fall back to its inline error state. However, bug 446328 is filed against plasmashell/general for Plasma's overall invalid-certificate UX: the reporter explicitly hit repeated modal dialogs from plasma-browser-integration as well as the weather widget, and Nate kept it open as a general Plasma UX issue. Closing BUG: 446328 while leaving other background KIO fetchers in kdeplasma-addons (POTD, comic, media frame) and plasma-browser-integration unfixed—and dismissing browser integration as non-Plasma—makes the fix incomplete.
changes: Extend ssl_no_ui suppression to the other background Plasma KIO fetchers rather than only the weather ions—at minimum the remaining kdeplasma-addons background fetchers (Picture of the Day wallpaper providers, comic applet, media frame) and plasma-browser-integration (which is a KDE Plasma repo and was specifically reported in comments 0 and 5).

Alternatively, consider suppressing or redirecting KIO's modal SSL dialog centrally for background jobs in plasmashell (e.g., via a custom KIO AskUserActionInterface / JobUiDelegateFactory or non-modal notification) so all Plasma widgets and wallpapers are covered consistently.

reviews.text: Setting ssl_no_ui on every weather-ion request is correct (KIO's http worker honors it, all eight KIO requests in the ions are covered) and the screenshots prove the dialog is gone for the weather widget. But the bug, as retitled by Nate, is about certificate-error UX in Plasma generally, not just the weather widget, and the notes themselves admit that other background fetchers in the same repo (Picture of the Day wallpaper providers, comic applet, media frame) still pop the same modal dialog from plasmashell on every refresh. As-is this only fixes one instance, so it can't carry BUG: 446328.
changes: Apply the same ssl_no_ui metadata to the other background KIO fetches in kdeplasma-addons (wallpapers/potd providers and the potd provider template, applets/comic/engine/comicprovider.cpp, applets/mediaframe/mediaframe.cpp) in this MR, and verify at least the POTD wallpaper on the rig with the same untrusted-certificate shim.

Update the commit message, line and explanation to cover all Plasma background fetchers, not only the weather widget; if any remaining path (e.g. the reporter's Discover/KNewStuff cases) is left out, state why it no longer shows a modal dialog in Plasma 6 or use CCBUG instead of BUG.
